title: Compound-v2 empty-market donation/rounding exposure in surviving forks
closed_reasons: Midas fMIMO-3 (Polygon) + fGLINT-0 (Moonbeam): T=0, CF>0, mint open, but the comptroller risk engine enforces minBorrowEth=143.919681304257721877 vs only $5.86/$0.38 of unpaused cash - borrowWithinLimits rejects every borrow large enough to matter

OCP kCake-LP (BSC): totalSupply=1 owned by another holder; the attacker cannot own the supply, so the truncating redeem leaves zero collateral (INSUFFICIENT_SHORTFALL); max theoretical gain with a 1-wei supply is CF*cash0/2 ~ $0
Paxo vLINK (Polygon): cToken implementation has no borrow(uint256) or redeemUnderlying(uint256) selectors - calls hit the fallback and revert
Sonne soVELO (Optimism): comptroller redeemVerify reverts 'redeemTokens zero' (the exact truncation guard)
Onyx: all markets collateralFactor=0 and mint/borrow guardian-paused (Ethereum block 26110123)
Scream: cash-bearing markets paused; the only unpaused listings (scFBTC/scFETH) have no contract code
Hundred: empty CF>0 unpaused markets exist but comptroller holds only dust cash (10,000,000,000,004 wei); Arbitrum hWBTC cash=0
Compound v2 itself: huge totalSupply -> free pull per call ~$2.5e-10
Starlay/Geist/Valas/Voltage/Ironclad: Aave forks, out of the cToken class
Resupply: share-market, hack already realized; zkLend: dead (Starknet)
key_facts: Core rule proven on forks: the borrow attack requires totalSupply==0. A market with even 1 wei of supply held by someone else is not exploitable (the attacker cannot burn the other holder's token; the truncating redeem leaves zero collateral)

Second rule proven on forks: a T=0 market with CF>0 and open mint is only exploitable if the protocol's borrow rules allow a large enough borrow; Midas enforces minBorrowEth=143.92 against $5.86 of cash

Universe: 263 comptrollers / 104 protocol families from DefiLlama's Compound-fork registry + corpus names; 220 read OK (2,124 markets), 24 bricked, 18 no-RPC chains; 14 markets pass the mechanical T=0+CF>0+mint-open predicate, all closed by the gates above

Closest near-misses: OCP/BSC $183,288.30 (closed by T=1 ownership), Paxo/Polygon $150.10 (closed by removed cToken functions), Midas dust $6.24 (closed by minBorrowEth), Sonne $50.30 direct-drain (closed by redeemVerify)
Direct-drain candidates are economically dead or guarded: Sonne soVELO T=13 with $50.30 (guard), Hundred/Arbitrum hWBTC T=2.0M wei with cash=0
Compound forum thread 4266 (2023) confirms the precondition (low total supply + non-zero collateral factor); the recommended fix is list with CF=0, mint, then set CF
caveats: Read-only snapshot at the listed blocks; guardians/admins can pause, set CF=0 or change borrow rules at any time
18 chain configs had no reachable public RPC and were not scanned (listed in ci-out/scan_summary.json)
24 comptrollers reverted getAllMarkets() (bricked/unverified); 1 chain hit the scan budget
The raw scan exposure numbers are mechanical preconditions; the fork tests/gates are the actual verdict (see README)
USD values use DefiLlama spot prices at scan time
one_liner: external unprivileged attacker can extract $0 live from the Compound-v2 empty-market/truncation class: all 14 mechanically eligible markets are closed by verified gates (Midas minBorrowEth 143.92 vs $5.86 cash, Paxo cToken has no borrow/redeemUnderlying, OCP T=1 supply owned by others) and every corpus target is paused/CF=0/phantom/guarded
